questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

Of all the forts (1)/ that I’ve visit in India, (2)/ Daulatabad Fort is my favourite. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that:

 
• The error lies in the second part of the sentence. 
 
• From the context of the sentence, we can infer that the person has already visited the places. 
 
• Therefore the given sentence is in the **past tense. **
 
• Thus the verb **visit** in the second part is wrong and should be changed to **visited**. 
 
• The verb **visited **makes the sentence grammatically correct. 

Therefore from the above points we can conclude that the correct answer is **2 **as the error lies in the second part. 

The correct sentence will be: *Of all the forts that I've **visited** in India, Daulatabad Fort is my favourite. *

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

The Bench will also have to say (1)/ whether the laws are really at consonance with (2)/ the basic tenets of the 1960 Act. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that:

**Whether **is used incorrectly in the given sentence. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

 
• **Whether **can be used only when two contrasting conditions are explicitly mentioned. 
 
• **Example**: Whether he will **go or not**. 
 
• In the given sentence we don't have two contrasting conditions. 
 
• Therefore the correct word to be used here is **if**. 

Thus from the above points we can conclude that the error lies in part **2 **of the sentence and therefore it is the correct answer. 

The correct sentence will be: *The Bench will also have to say **if **the laws are really at consonance with the basic tenets of the 1960 Act. *

• **'Carouse' **is a **verb **and it means **'to enjoy yourself by drinking alcohol and speaking and laughing loudly in a group of people'** so that the similar word of** 'Carouse' **is **'Quaff'**. It is the most suitable option here.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in ****correct**** order.**

Sociologists believe

P: that the reason why honour killings

Q: of the continued rigidity of the caste system

R: continue to take place is because
questions.solution:
*Believe of *= grammatically incorrect phrase. *Believe in something* or ***believe something*** would be correct. Thus, Q can't be first. Similarly, *believe continue *is incorrect too => only P can be first. Rule out 2) and 3). R can't be last since a sentence can't end with **because** =. rule out 4). Option 1) *PRQ *is the correct answer.

**Sociologists believe that the reason why honour killings continue to take place is because of the continued rigidity of the caste system. **

questions.question:
A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

The visitor enquired, “When is the next train?”

options.text: The visitor enquired about the next train.
The visitor enquired when the next train was.
The visitor asked when is the next train.
The visitor was interested in the next train.

questions.solution:
No part of the information should be deleted in reported speech. Since the visitor is interested in knowing **when** i.e. time related, we can't eliminate that part => rule out 1) and 4). Simple present tense (when is) => simple past (**was**). option 2) *The visitor enquired when the next train was *is the correct answer.

Notice how **was **has been moved to the end of the sentence. It is usually done when you change a question* *to a statement.

questions.question: Left to itself, then, attention _____________ obeys natural laws
questions.solution:
The correct answer is-** 'Simply'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Here, word **'obeys'** is a **verb**. So, the blank must contain an **adverb** to describe the verb.
 
• **'Simply'** is an adverb here. So, simply is the** only **possible choice.
 
• **'Simple'** is an adjective here. So, it is** not** the correct answer.
 
• **'Simplification' **and **'Simplicity'** are nouns here. So, it is also **not** the correct answer.
 
• So, according to above explanation adverb **'Simply'** is the correct answer.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is-* Left to itself, then, attention** simply** obeys natural laws.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are some words that end with** '-ly'** but are** not adverbs.**

questions.question: conscious of effort _____________ struggle to compel
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Nor'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Nor' is used to connect two negative clauses in a sentence, creating a parallel negative structure without the need to repeat the negation word such as "not."
 
• In the given sentence structure, "conscious of effort" represents the first negative scenario. The conjunction 'Nor' effectively introduces the second negative component "struggle to compel us to cease thinking about this thing and begin thinking about that."
 
• The correct use of 'Nor' in this context highlights the absence of both effort and struggle, emphasizing that the flow of thoughts is undirected and effortless.
 
• This usage adheres to the correct grammatical rule for pairing negative constructs, where 'Nor' is the appropriate choice to link two ideas or conditions that are both lacking.
 
• The choice of 'Nor' facilitates a smooth and logical continuation of the idea being expressed in the sentence, ensuring clarity and coherence in the message about the nature of unforced attention and thought.
 
• The overall sentence with 'Nor' correctly filled in emphasizes how thought can proceed without conscious control or opposition, in a natural and unobstructed manner.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'No' is primarily used as a determiner or adverb but does not function correctly to connect two negative clauses.
 
• 'Not' is used to make a clause negative but cannot link two negative clauses in the way required for the sentence structure.
 
• 'None' is a pronoun referring to 'not one' or 'not any' and doesn't suit the structure that requires a conjunction.
 
• Understanding the correct use of 'Nor' in context is essential for proper sentence construction, especially in formal or written English where precision is crucial.
